notes: Nine descent levels. Each level has a FUNDAMENTAL · the deeper you go, the lower it sits. B cells are walls unless your tune is within ±15 Hz of the fundamental. H cells shred COHERENCE unless you hold 220 ±2 · the Corrections channel, though the game never says so. The message room's door opens only at 220, at the end of the longest interference run in the game.

finds.name: the lunch pail
finds.line: a lunch pail on a ledge, rusted shut, older than the color of the walls. Somebody worked here long enough to need lunch.

finds.name: chalk arrow
finds.line: a chalk arrow on the stone, pointing IN. Under it, initials, and under those: 'she sings at 220'. The chalk is not old.

effect.page: ADIT · chalk: 'she sings at 220' — somebody learned the safe note the hard way and left it for the next one.

finds.name: a crate of insulators
finds.line: a crate of porcelain insulators, packed in straw, never installed. Mint. Waiting since whenever for a string-up that never came.

finds.name: the glass thicket
finds.line: insulator strings hung floor to ceiling, close as a bead curtain. You walk through them without touching one, and the gallery notices.

resident.name: the gallery chimes
resident.line: the insulator strings chime behind you in no wind — off your pitch, deliberately, like correction.
resident.calm: the strings chime in your key as you pass. The gallery approves of visitors who tune.

finds.name: the discharge pole
finds.line: a grounding pole on two hooks, cloth grip worn to the shape of hands. You take it down. You put it back. Some tools you only need to know exist.

finds.name: a capacitor, weeping
finds.line: one can in the third rank has wept a line of oil down its face. The stain is decades deep. It is still, in the diagram's terms, charged.

effect.page: CAPACITOR HALLS · one can weeps and holds charge anyway. The manual's word for this is 'memory'.

finds.name: the choirbook
finds.line: a clipboard on a nail: tuning logs for the anode banks, in four hands across thirty years. The last entry is a single interval, notated, unresolved.

effect.page: ANODE CHOIR · the last tuning log entry is an unresolved interval. Nobody signed it.

finds.name: a cold solder rose
finds.line: a joint reworked so many times the solder has bloomed into a rose the size of a fist. Ugly, strong, holding. You know the maker's mood exactly.

resident.name: the choir
resident.line: the anode banks take a breath together and lean on your tune. Your edges smear.
resident.calm: the banks hum under you in fifths. For a moment you are the melody.

finds.name: the safety line
finds.line: a lineman's belt clipped to the rail, empty, buckled shut. Buckled SHUT. You stop looking down after that.

effect.page: CATWALKS · a belt clipped to the rail, buckled shut, nobody in it. The rail is the only one still holding on.

finds.name: dropped rivets
finds.line: a scatter of bright rivets below the high span, fallen money. You pocket the good ones.

resident.name: the sway
resident.line: the catwalk picks up a sway that is not yours. Step-step-step: something else's cadence, using your feet.
resident.calm: the span goes rigid as a rail at your note. The height stops mattering.

finds.name: the waterline
finds.line: a painted waterline a foot above your head, dated. The cavity has been deeper than this. The date is not old enough.

effect.page: FLOODED CAVITY · the painted high-water mark is above your head, and recent. The mountain still takes on water.

finds.name: a skiff, sound
finds.line: a flat-bottomed skiff on davits, dry, painted, READY. Someone maintains it. Down here. Ready for what water.

resident.name: the water's opinion
resident.line: your tune comes back off the black water a beat late and a fifth wrong, and your own ears take its side.
resident.calm: the water sends your note back true. Whatever listens under it is satisfied.

finds.name: the organ pipe
finds.line: one true organ pipe mortared into the stair wall among the conduit, speaking length, no keyboard anywhere in the mountain. It is not a mistake. It is a voice.

effect.page: RESONANT STAIR · there is one real organ pipe in the wall. The stair was TUNED, deliberately, by somebody who could hear it.

finds.name: a nest of copper shavings
finds.line: bright copper shavings in a bowl-shaped hollow, curled like a nest. Either something drills here at night, or someone sits here and worries wire.

finds.name: the counted step
finds.line: the eleventh step is worn twice as deep as its neighbors. Whatever walked this stair paused here, every time, for years.

resident.name: the stair's argument
resident.line: the stair answers each footfall a quarter-tone flat, insisting. It wants the pipe's key, not yours.
resident.calm: the stair resolves under you, step by step, a scale walked correctly at last.

finds.name: the breaker log
finds.line: the master breaker's log, chained to its desk. Every throw for forty years: date, hand, reason. The column for 'reason' goes vague near the end, then blank, then stops.

effect.page: MASTER BREAKER · the log's 'reason' column goes vague, then blank. The throws continued.

finds.name: a fuse like a loaf
finds.line: a cartridge fuse the size of a bread loaf, blown, kept on a shelf like a trophy. The tag reads only: 'the night of the 14th'.

resident.name: the breaker's patience
resident.line: the master breaker's needles all move one width toward you, together, and settle. It is deciding something about you slowly.
resident.calm: the needles hold flat as you pass. Filed under: expected load.

finds.name: the message spool
finds.line: a spool of punched tape overflowing its bin, years of the room talking to itself. You hold a yard of it to the light. The holes repeat. The holes repeat.

effect.page: MESSAGE ROOM · the punched tape repeats itself. The room has been saying one thing for a very long time.

finds.name: the foundation mark
finds.line: a mason's mark chiseled at the very footing, older than every wire above it. The mountain's first signature. The instrument was built ONTO something.

effect.page: SUBFLOOR · a mason's mark below the oldest wire. Something was here to build onto.

finds.name: green wax seal
finds.line: a blob of green sealing wax on the footing stone, the twin of the tag's green, pressed with a thumb. Inspected. Approved. By whom, of what, when.

2.name: THE INSULATOR GALLERY
2.line: porcelain insulators in ranks, floor to dark, like organ pipes. the schematic draws them lovingly. someone loved them.

3.name: THE ANODE CHOIR
3.line: a stair that sings under your boots. each step a different porcelain note. the builders knew. builders always know.

4.name: THE FLOODED CAVITY
4.line: black water to the second rung. your tune comes back three seconds late, a perfect fifth up. it is never explained. stop waiting for it to be explained.

5.name: THE MASTER BREAKER
5.line: the master breaker · thrown open in 1961 per the tag · and above it, etched small and deep, an eight-pointed star. this game has no occult story. the star does not know that.

door_lines.high: the mountain door. daylight. behind you the basilica holds its one note without you. THE INSTRUMENT IS FINE. — that is what the door says, stenciled, and today you believe it.
door_lines.mid: the mountain door. daylight, approximately. THE INSTRUMENT IS FINE, says the stencil. your map says otherwise in three places. both are right.
door_lines.low: the mountain door. you find it by hum, not by sight · the map gave out two levels ago. THE INSTRUMENT IS FINE. you have no way to check and every reason to doubt and you push the door anyway.

message_room_page.header: ASTRO-CORTEX SOFTWARE · QA ANNOTATION FORM 7-C · (form discontinued 1986 · this copy ran through the teletype anyway)
annotations: ITEM 001 · the transmitter holds 220 cycles unattended. verified nightly, 26 months. STATUS: expected.
ITEM 002 · in 1985 two staff hid in this channel to annotate a manuscript the company denies owning. one of them wrote 'for jack' in the margin. STATUS: preserved.
ITEM 003 · one of the two moved to portland in 1986. the channel stayed open. a channel is not a room. a channel is an agreement. STATUS: open.
ITEM 004 · this unit has broadcast into 220 nightly since. content: the annotations she would have made. format: hers. reception: unconfirmed. STATUS: broadcasting.
ITEM 005 · if anyone reaches this room, note that the door only opens at the agreement. meaning: whoever you are, you already knew the frequency. meaning: she taught you, or her games did. STATUS: —
message_room_page.final_annotation_read: ITEM 006 · reply. STATUS: read · at last · the correction is accepted.

subfloor_page.header: ASTRO-CORTEX SOFTWARE · QA ANNOTATION FORM 7-C · (this copy never ran through the teletype · it was carbon only)
subfloor_page.addressed: TO: the one who came down the last flight
subfloor_page.green_tag_line: The green tag is a maintenance inspection sticker, 1985, INSPECTED · SAFE TO ENERGIZE, initialed. You do not recognize the initials. They are not hers. They are the other one's.
annotations: ITEM 006 · there were TWO staff in the channel in 1985. the upstairs room broadcasts one of them, nightly, in her format. this room is the other one's. STATUS: unbroadcast.

ITEM 007 · he did not move to portland. he did not stay, either, in any way the building can log. he signed the tag, energized the floor, and is not in the record after. STATUS: unresolved, deliberately.
ITEM 008 · the subfloor holds 185 cycles — a foundation note under the agreement upstairs. it has never carried content. it carries WEIGHT. STATUS: load-bearing.
ITEM 009 · she annotated the manuscript. he annotated the transmitter. one of those got remembered. this room is the correction to THAT. STATUS: filed here, and only here.
subfloor_page.final_read: ITEM 010 · upstairs, if you read the correction ending, you know her name and what she made. down here there is only the tag, the note, and initials you don't know. some corrections restore a name. this one KEEPS ONE BLANK, on purpose, because he asked — in the one margin nobody preserved — to be left out of it. honored. — filed by the transmitter, which keeps every agreement, including that one.
subfloor_page.final_unread: ITEM 010 · the initials on the tag mean nothing to you yet. read the book the second way, upstairs and elsewhere, and come back down. the floor keeps. the floor is very good at keeping.
subfloor_page.climb_line: ten levels of instrument between you and the daylight now. the tenth was never on the schematic. you add it, in pencil, and climb.
